=== adjudicate-term
usage: db.py adjudicate-term [-h] --observation-id OBSERVATION_ID
                             --outcome {DEFERRED,NAMES-EXISTING,NAMES-NEW,NOT-OURS}
                             [--term-id TERM_ID] --rationale RATIONALE
                             --session SESSION [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --observation-id OBSERVATION_ID
  --outcome {DEFERRED,NAMES-EXISTING,NAMES-NEW,NOT-OURS}
                        Live vocabulary, read from the column's own CHECK
  --term-id TERM_ID     Required for NAMES-EXISTING; refused otherwise. NAMES-
                        NEW is written only by `add-term --from-observation`,
                        and this verb refuses --outcome NAMES-NEW
  --rationale RATIONALE
                        Why. An adjudication that cannot be contested is not
                        one.
  --session SESSION
  --dry-run
=== add-term
usage: db.py add-term [-h] --from-observation FROM_OBSERVATION
                      --canonical-en CANONICAL_EN --rationale RATIONALE
                      [--definition DEFINITION] [--domain DOMAIN]
                      [--scope-note SCOPE_NOTE]
                      [--distinct-from DISTINCT_FROM] --session SESSION
                      [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --from-observation FROM_OBSERVATION
                        observed_terms.observation_id the term is minted FROM
  --canonical-en CANONICAL_EN
                        the parameter's name — never a value, never a
                        comparator
  --rationale RATIONALE
                        why this phrase names a concept we did not hold
  --definition DEFINITION
  --domain DOMAIN
  --scope-note SCOPE_NOTE
  --distinct-from DISTINCT_FROM
                        repeatable: a TERM-ID the writer reports as a near
                        match (shared tokens) that this concept is NOT; the
                        --rationale says why. Without it a near match is
                        refused
  --session SESSION
  --dry-run
=== add-parameter
usage: db.py add-parameter [-h] --term-id TERM_ID [--notes NOTES]
                           --session SESSION [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --term-id TERM_ID  terms.term_id. Refused if absent, declined, value-bearing
                     or already a parameter. A NAMES-NEW/NAMES-EXISTING
                     adjudication is REPORTED as provenance, not required

options:

  --slug SLUG
  --ref REF
  --direction {backward,forward}
  --deferred-reason DEFERRED_REASON
                        Why this anchor was NOT mined -- DELIBERATELY NOT
                        SEARCHED (R6). Never a findings channel: if the pass
                        RAN, use --notes.
  --notes NOTES         What a pass that RAN found, including nothing. Writes
                        citation_mining.notes, which existed with no writer
                        until 2026-09-18. APPENDS -- it never overwrites an
                        earlier pass's note. Mutually exclusive with
                        --deferred-reason.
  --discharge-deferral  Assert that the deferral standing on this row belongs
                        to the direction just run, and clear it (its text is
                        carried into notes, never destroyed). NOT automatic,
                        and that is the point: deferred_reason is ONE column
                        while backward and forward are TWO, so a backward pass
                        cannot tell whether the standing deferral was its own.
                        Without this flag the deferral stands and the result
                        says so.
  --status MINING_STATUS
                        citation_mining_status to set on the source. Live
                        vocabulary from the column's own CHECK. Derived when
                        omitted: 'deferred' with --deferred-reason, 'mined'
                        otherwise -- so an executed zero-yield pass (--notes)
                        derives 'mined', which is the 2026-09-18 ruling that
                        executed IS mined. This help said "'mined' with
                        connections, 'deferred' without" until that day, which
                        described neither the code nor the ruling.

G SW P2 'The source marks every statement as Code (required) or Best Practice by text colour (legend on its PDF p. 1), and the figure-level distinction it draws (for example item 1.2: the path is Code, the 1500 mm minimum width is Best Practice) has no typed column on source_value_extractions. It was recorded in notes only (REF-01037 extractions). Found by REF-01037; a schema question for a tooling pull request.'
G SW P3 'log-search demands a subject (--slug, --parameter or --mined-ref-id) even for --origin owner-supplied, where no search ran; REF-01037 was logged against parameter 3 only to satisfy the writer. Also log-mining cannot record a deferred forward direction once the backward pass has set citation_mining_status to mined (GAP-015, GAP-022 unruled). Found while admitting REF-01037.'
G DEC P2 'Does the source colour contrast (the source requires it at many elements, with no figure) name the catalogue LRV contrast concept? Adjudicated DEFERRED on REF-01037 (observed term colour contrast); the owner decides whether it is TERM-011 or a distinct concept.'
G DEC P2 'Which identity code states a figure when the item names no group: REF-01037 figures for ramp slope, corridor width, headroom and landing interval were tagged ALL on the warrant "meet the needs of all users" (the source purpose statement on its PDF p. 1), and the door width and turning figures MOB on the source own sentence about wheelchairs and scooters. The owner or the lens ruling confirms or corrects these tags.' --identity ALL
G EG P2 'REF-01037 states figures and requirements for many concepts the catalogue holds no parameter for, adjudicated DEFERRED and not minted (OR-17 leaves minting to the data pull request the owner reads). Derive the list: select o.surface_form, o.locator from observed_terms o join term_adjudications a using (observation_id) where o.ref_id = "REF-01037" and a.outcome = "DEFERRED".'
G EG P3 'REF-01037 is a City of Edmonton document and its figures are recorded under country code CA: base_jurisdictions holds no sub-national code for Alberta or Edmonton (T-024 built the registry; add-jurisdiction admits one with an approval reference).' --jurisdiction CA
G RP P2 'Backward-mining leads named by REF-01037 and staged REFERENCE-ONLY, not retrieved: the Safety Codes Council Barrier-Free Design Guide (Aug 2019 PDF), the City of Edmonton Access Design Guide, Policy C602, and the Alberta Building Code (no edition stated). The Barrier-Free Design Guide and the Alberta code edition are the likely holders of the dimensions REF-01037 asserts; derive the leads: select ref_id, title from source_locators where recovered_from like "REF-01037%".'
G SW P3 'REF-01037 text defects as printed, recorded without correction: item 6.2 "With the ramp at any point shall not be less than 1500mm/60" has no subject noun (it reads like a ramp width); item 5.3 gives "at least 910 - 915mm" and "1500x1500mm" turning radius; item 2.10 prints a corridor width under the entrances heading; item 4.7 and 7.1 repeat the handrail rule. Extractions 236 and 237 carry the ambiguity in notes. A reviewer reads the page render before relying on them.' --parameter 9

argument-hint: "[what to attack — a diff, a batch, a document]"
---

Run the pair. Do not let one model check its own work; that is the failure this
exists to prevent.

**0. No agent-launching tool?** Say so in your handback and stop. Do not run the
antagonist's checklist yourself and call it a pass — batch 20 did exactly that ("the
authoring subagent had no agent-launching tool, so it ran a self-administered pass")
and it "missed every one of the independent pass's findings." A self-administered pass
is not a pass, and `db.py record-adversarial-pass` refuses one whose reviewer and
author transcripts are the same file (RC4).

**1. Critic.** Before launching it, capture `SUBJECT_COMMIT="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` — the
sha the reviewer will actually read. Capturing it AFTER step 2's repair names the wrong
commit (the repaired state, not what was reviewed). Launch the `antagonist` agent
(Fable, read-only) against: $1

It attacks the claim. It does not summarize the work, and it does not propose
the repair — proposing a fix is how a critic talks itself into accepting the
thing. Require of it:

- every finding names the artifact and the line, and states the failure case
- a finding that a gate "should" have caught is checked against whether that gate
  had a SUBJECT — a check that passed having examined nothing is this
  repository's most-produced defect (CLAUDE.md §5a)
- every count it cites is one it just computed
- `[NULL: <scope> — examined, nothing found]` where it found nothing, rather than
  silence

**2. Adjudicate, then repair.** Take its findings one at a time. For each: confirm
it against the artifact yourself, then fix or reject with a reason. A finding you
cannot reproduce is not a finding — say so and move on.

**3. Record the pass (RC4).** Once the critic's transcript is committed (rule 6) and
carries the closing ` ```json adversarial-findings ``` ` block, on a SCRATCH copy of the
DB (CLAUDE.md §4 — this writer, like every db.py subcommand, refuses to open the
canonical DB read-write):

```
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$SCRATCH python3 scripts/db.py record-adversarial-pass \
  --subject-session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)" --subject-commit "$SUBJECT_COMMIT" \
  --reviewer-transcript transcripts/<...>/<critic-transcript>.jsonl \
  --author-transcript transcripts/<...>/<your-own-transcript>.jsonl \
  --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
```

The row then travels the ordinary write path (emit_batch_sql → emit_data_migration →
migrate_db) with the rest of this batch's rows — it is research data (RC6), not tooling,
and ships in the batch's data migration, never hand-applied to the canonical DB.

Then, for each finding: `db.py dispose-adversarial-finding --finding-id N --disposition
REPAIRED|REJECTED|PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED|OWNER-RULED [--ref ... | --reason ...]` — REPAIRED
names the data migration path that fixed it; OWNER-RULED names the exact ledger quote,
occurring once. Finally `db.py close-adversarial-pass --pass-id N --session ...`, which
refuses until every lens is covered and at least one row is SURVIVED. **Never run it on
pass 1:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-27 (second, `references/project-standards.md`,
ACTION (2)) holds pass 1 OPEN. Pass 2 was left open by its own session and the
process-gap plan approved 2026-10-01 keeps it open. Nothing refuses either; you are the
gate. A finding admitted only on the database file is closed but printed as REPORTED:
the database is not an artefact of attack.

**4. Gate before claiming done.**

```
scripts/preflight.sh
python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest      # mandatory after ANY rename
```

Report the findings and their disposition. Do not report the critique as the
deliverable — the repair is the deliverable.
['L1-existence', 'L2-fidelity', 'L3-independence', 'L4-tier', 'L5-population', 'L6-contrary', 'L7-recognition', 'L8-query-shape', 'S1-harm-reached-row', 'S2-mismatch-note-vs-payload', 'S3-containment', 'S4-sequence']

The digest has gone through every pipeline stage on a scratch copy of the database, and an independent critic is now attacking it. The canonical database was not touched. I'm waiting on the critic's report, and the cluster C authoring agent is still running.

**What the pass did, in order:**
- **Admission:** REF-01037 (tier 3 grey, owner-supplied) was admitted as VERIFIED after a persisted fetch and a read of all nine rendered pages and the text layer.
- **Observations:** 55 phrases were adjudicated. 23 named existing terms and 32 were deferred; none were minted. 14 element terms were declined as parameters, and two (level threshold, intermediate landing) were promoted.
- **Extractions:** 16 figures against parameters 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14, each with a lens link. The source marks every statement as Code (required, blue) or Best Practice (magenta), and I read that from the text-layer colour and checked it against the renders.
- **Scans, leads and gaps:** the full-text scans are recorded (nine of nine pages), four backward-mining leads staged, two follow-ups raised and eight gaps filed.
- **Engine and checks:** all ten cells it reached come out pending, because a grey tier-3 source can't anchor a determination alone. The research definition-of-done check is compliant. K01 and K02 examine 10 live rows on the scratch copy, and the batch SQL captured by `emit_batch_sql.py` is ready but not applied or committed.

Cluster A's report also found that `test_run_pipeline_refusals` (X02, X03) now fails. Those tests use REF-01037 as a throwaway fixture id, and my derived text for the real REF-01037 now sits in the retrieval log, so the tests' `--verbatim-exempt` case is refused. That is a latent defect: once this batch is merged, the real REF-01037 will break those fixtures for good. It needs a tooling task that has the fixtures derive a free id.

Clusters A and B of the authoring are done: T-061, T-062 and T-063, then T-067 to T-072. I'll integrate the index rows and push once cluster C reports. I'll then write the full document of what the digest did.

## 2. How it was run (the pipeline's own order)

**The document.** It is a 9-page City of Edmonton Accessibility Advisory Committee checklist with 75 numbered items. It prints no date. The stored year, 2022, comes from the PDF's creation metadata.

Two things in the payload would be missed by a text-only reading. First, the document marks every statement as Code (required, blue) or Best Practice (magenta), and the text layer drops that distinction. I recovered it from the text colour and checked it against the page renders. Second, the legend names four access categories (Physical, Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Blind or Low Vision, Cognitive) in white text on a white page, so they are invisible when rendered, and no item carries a group tag.

**What the digest produced** (the pipeline's `from-evidence` variant, on a scratch database):
- **Admission and reading:** REF-01037 was admitted as tier 3 grey (marker ○), with the source's colour-coding recorded in each extraction's notes. All nine pages and the derived text were read at full scope.
- **Observations:** 86 phrases were observed and adjudicated. 23 name existing terms and 57 are deferred. None were minted, because the owner reads minting in the data pull request.
- **Parameters:** 14 element terms were declined, and two were promoted (parameters 13 and 14) because the source states a figure for them.
- **Extractions:** 16, against parameters 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14, including two absent findings for LRV contrast and operating force.
- **Engine and gate:** all ten cells it could compute come out pending, because a grey tier-3 source cannot anchor a value. The research definition-of-done check is compliant. K01 and K02 examined the ten engine-written cells and passed.

**Corrections and limits (section 7 of the report):**
- I first treated the admission as a research find and ran a Crossref search. The PDF is owner-supplied, so it is now logged as such.
- The first scan note overclaimed that every requirement phrase had been observed. I then did the remaining 31 observations, so the claim is true now.
- Nothing is committed. No migration was written, there is no forward citation pass and no Co-1 pass, and the adversarial pass isn't recorded in the database.

**Needs your decision (section 6 of the report):**
- Whether grey tier 3 is the right classification for this kind of document.
- Whether `ALL` and `MOB` are the right lens tags where an item names no group.
- Which of the 57 deferred concepts become parameters.
- Whether the document's "colour contrast" is the catalogue's LRV contrast.

**The test failure to fix before shipping.** The derived text I registered under REF-01037 makes `test_run_pipeline_refusals` cases X02 and X03 fail, because they use REF-01037 as a throwaway fixture id. That will break permanently once the real source lands, so the fixtures need to derive a free id.

The antagonist critic is still running. Its findings and my disposition of each will be appended to section 9 of the report when it returns.

content.text:
The loop already exists, but it is open at the end, so the base only grows where a task such to T-072 is aimed. What follows is read from the pipeline skill and T-072, T-020, T-028 and T-105, not from a new design.

**The mechanism today**
1. **Harvest.** Every reading records each concept phrase the source uses (`observe-term`, verbatim, with its sentence and locator). This is R11 and costs nothing extra.
2. **Adjudicate.** Each observation gets an answer: names an existing term, is not ours, or is deferred. A term is minted only from an observation, and only in the source's own words, never a phrase I generate (OR-17, E1).
3. **Promote or decline.** A concept the source states a figure for becomes a parameter (`add-parameter`). Otherwise it is declined with a reason. Terms can also be renamed and parameters merged, so the base can shrink.
4. **Re-read debt is automatic.** A new parameter widens the catalogue version, and `v_scan_ledger` then owes a targeted re-read of every held source (T-072 states this).
5. **Guards.** Near-duplicates are refused, parameters stay flat and coarse (OD-24), and a new quantity kind needs a warrant (T-020).

**Where it stalls**
- **DEFERRED has no consumer.** Nothing in the plan revisits it. This PDF alone deferred 57 phrases.
- **T-072 only seeds from regulatory codes.** The other sources, such as grey, Co-1 and research papers, add phrases but never trigger minting.
- **No recurrence signal.** A phrase seen once looks the same as one seen in ten independent sources, so nothing ranks which to mint first.
- **Minting waits for a hand-built review.** OR-17 sends every batch to you in a data pull request, with no generated review sheet to read.
- **Pending cells don't feed back.** A cell that stays pending because a parameter is missing does not queue a candidate.

**What I'd build, in order of value**
1. **A derived candidate queue, not a curated list** (rule 8). It would group every unminted observation by phrase and concept, with the figures stated beside it, the number of independent sources, their tiers, and a locator for each. A phrase that recurs across independent sources with a stated figure ranks first.
2. **A generated review sheet.** The queue renders as the bulk document you read for each minting pull request: each candidate with quotes, sources and a proposed disposition of mint, alias, element or decline.
3. **A standing catalogue-growth batch.** This is T-072 widened from held codes to every DEFERRED or unadjudicated observation, run on a cadence or whenever the queue passes a threshold. It adds nothing new that it computes itself: it reads the queue and applies your decisions.
4. **A feedback hook from specification.** When a cell pends for a missing parameter, its gap writes a candidate observation back to the queue.

**Decisions for you**
- Is recurrence across independent sources enough to propose minting, with you still approving?
- Should an element-only phrase, with no figure, ever be mined, or stay an alias or decline?
- What cadence or threshold triggers a growth batch?

Say if you want a task file for 1 to 3. It would be a research task for the queue and sheet's content and a tooling task for the view and renderer, shipped in separate pull requests. For the decisions above I'd lean towards:
- recurrence as the ranking signal only;
- element-only phrases not mined;
- a growth batch whenever the queue holds a stated figure that no parameter takes.

    toks = re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", (name or "").lower())
    return frozenset(t[:-1] if len(t) > 3 and t.endswith("s") else t for t in toks)


def _near_terms(conn, name: str) -> list:
    """Terms whose canonical name or ATTESTED English alias shares a token set with `name` one
    way or the other (subset or superset): 'ramp runs' beside 'ramp run length',
    'reverberations' beside 'reverberation time'. The equivalence search the skill tells an
    operator to do before minting, done by the writer and refused unless each is named

    or owner_supplied alias is STILL compared, as before 130: E4 (whether a form without a
    locator is vocabulary) is an open owner question, and a live refusal is not weakened on
    the strength of an open question. The label comparison is unchanged."""
    want = _name_tokens(name)
    if not want:
        return []
    out, seen = [], set()

Both questions come down to the same test: a parameter is one measured quantity, and everything else about a figure (where it applies, under what condition, for whom) goes on the figure or the determination. The plan states this in OD-24, T-109 and the TERM-089 decline.

## Not duplicating

**What exists:**
- Before minting, `add-term` compares the new name against every term and every attested English alias (`_near_terms` in `db.py`). If their word sets nest, it refuses unless each match is named `--distinct-from` with a rationale.
- An exact name hit goes to the existing term.
- Aliases are typed (`SYNONYM`, `BROADER`, `NARROWER`, `TRANSLATION`, `DOMAIN`, `DEPRECATED`) and carry an attestation. An alias from a model seed does not block anything.
- `merge-parameter` and `rename-term` undo a duplicate after the fact.

**What it misses:**
- It compares words only, so it never catches a synonym with no shared token.
- It compares names only, not definitions, quantity kinds or units.
- It doesn't handle cross-language synonyms; those wait on E1, where an instrument's own phrase counts as the name.
- Equivalence is a recorded judgment with a rationale. In my digest, adjudicating "doorway clearance" as existing term TERM-021, door width, was one of those judgments, and it is contestable.

**What I'd add:** a derived candidate list beside each proposed term, ranked by overlap of name, definition, quantity kind, unit dimension and direction. This depends on T-020 (kinds) and T-028 (naming).

## Branch of a parameter versus its own

| Question about the figure | Answer | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| Same quantity (same kind and unit dimension, same better-direction), different circumstance | Same parameter | `--setting`, the lens, the device class, or an element pointer (T-060) |
| It applies only under a condition | A branch of the determination | A `condition_on` edge; T-017 keeps it out of the headline |
| Different quantity: width vs height vs length vs time vs count vs force | Its own parameter | A new parameter, even on the same element |
| A thing, not a measure | Declined as an element | `decline-parameter` (the TERM-089 `ramp` precedent) |
| A threshold that triggers a rule | A condition on that rule's figure, not a value of anything | `condition_on` |
| A passage in the source | Neither; clauses are what is read, not catalogue units | The clause inventory behind T-031 (OD-23) |

**Examples from the Edmonton PDF:**
- Path width (1500 mm, item 1.2) and corridor width (1100 mm, item 2.10) are one quantity in two settings: parameter 4.
- The elevator door's 910–915 mm is parameter 9 (door width) in an elevator setting.
- The 9 m landing interval is parameter 12, ramp run length.
- "Handrails on both sides if the stair is 1100 mm or wider" is a condition on a handrail rule, not a stair-width parameter.
- The access aisle's 1500 mm and 6000 mm are two quantities, width and length.

**One of my digest decisions fails this test.** I promoted TERM-092 `intermediate landing` and TERM-022 `level threshold` to parameters. Both names are elements, not quantities. A landing has a length, a width and a slope; a threshold has a height. That contradicts the `ramp` decline's own reasoning, which sends landings to a quantity and not to the element. I should have named the quantities (landing length, threshold rise) or left the figures unextracted.

I can undo those two promotions on the scratch database and reframe the two extractions; the digest hasn't shipped, so it costs nothing to fix. Say if you want that done.

The same weakness shows up in the plan:
- The `quantity_kind` check in T-020 doesn't stop a parameter being named for an element.
- Nothing yet distinguishes the measured thing from the element it sits on until T-060.

I'd put the test above into the candidate review sheet as per-candidate fields: kind, unit dimension, direction, element, setting. A parameter named for an element would then fail on sight.

content.content:
OD-24: flat and coarse; kinds = length, gradient (ratio, percentage or degrees as notations), force, time, luminous reflectance and its contrast (LRV), colour temperature, held as rows and extended by data with a warrant; element required: no

**The resolution.** A parameter is one measured quantity, with every clause variation a typed condition and families reached by typed term pointers; two cases are two parameters only when they cannot be placed on one scale or their accessibility directions differ. Clause-level extractions are kept and reached by pointer. Each parameter states its quantity kind from a registry of kinds held as rows (seeded from what the live parameters need, not from a list typed in code) and extended by data with a warrant. A parameter need not belong to an element; elements reach parameters by term pointers, many to many.

**What decided it.** The owner's statement of 2026-11-12 (second) that too fine a grain loses the commonality needed to "unify then specify". Criterion 1: one determination per quantity, no parent and child values to keep in step. Criterion 2: one value with its conditions. Criterion 3: group differences ride on lenses, and opposite directions split. Requiring an element would recreate the container the owner deleted.

**Reversal condition.** A parameter whose cases share a scale and direction but cannot be determined together without losing a group's difference, or a kind that cannot be added without a schema change.

CONDITION: any session defining, splitting, merging or typing a parameter, or adding a quantity kind.
ACTION: (1) Keep parameters flat and coarse; apply the split test. (2) Carry variations as typed conditions. (3) State a kind from the kinds registry; add a kind by data with a warrant. (4) Require no element.
====
Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "recognize that we need to approach parameters from a higher level abstract vantage as too many clauses and subclauses means we may lose commonality and therefore can't unify then specify"

**What this records.** The grain at which a parameter is defined is to be abstract enough that clauses and subclauses from different instruments and jurisdictions remain comparable; defined too finely, the commonality is lost and nothing can be unified, so nothing can be specified. The order named is unify, then specify.

**What it does not decide.** How the abstraction is represented (a parent/child or family relation, an equivalence group, a coarser parameter list), who judges a grouping, and how clause-level traceability is kept under a coarser parameter are open. It touches the 2026-08-26 ruling that the judgment object is the canonical parameter and the 2026-10-09 statement that the parameter list is seeded from the existing terms; neither is superseded by this entry. The first two questions have mostly built answers; the third is settled doctrine with an open representation question. All three are read from the ledger, `specifications` and the plan.

**Different values for different groups and design modes**
- **Separate cells, not mixed values.** A determination is one parameter combined with its lens codes: identity, access need, ICF or medical, at least one. A figure reaches a cell only through its own live lens links (T-019), so a value for `MOB` and one for `BLIND` sit in different cells and never blend. The two cell states are `pending` and `provisional`.
- **Disagreement between groups.** A parameter whose direction is `contested` shows the spread, with each population's direction, and never one invented value. A conflict goes in `add-conflict`.
- **Design mode.** `specifications.design_scale` takes `universal`, `population` or `person`. The engine writes `universal` when only code-stratum (T4–T6) evidence stands behind the cell, and `population` otherwise. The cell is then the code floor, never best practice, as the Universal Mode doctrine fixes. `person` is OT-assessed: the guidebook gives no values and no person-assessment form.
- **A gap.** I found no rule that derives a universal value from the per-group cells. It exists only where code evidence alone stands.

**Commercial, residential, public**
- **Ruled, not built.** On 2026-08-27 you ruled that `base_building` has three levels: building type (residential, commercial), room type and construction element. The `rooms` table (17 rows) exists and the other two levels are absent. The building-type level is also deferred in the conceptual model (ENT-16).
- **Handling today.** It lives as free text in each figure's `setting`. Nothing keys or filters a cell by it, so a dwellings figure and a non-dwellings figure for the same parameter and lens can land in one determination.
- **The doctrine on variation.** OD-24 says carry such variations as typed conditions, not separate parameters. T-017 turns a conditioned claim into a branch, kept out of the headline. What is missing is the typed vocabulary and the registry.
- **"Public"** is the instrument's own legal scope word, and it differs by country.

**Too granular versus too encompassing**
- **The split test (OD-24).** Two cases are two parameters only when they cannot be placed on one scale, or their accessibility directions differ. Everything else is one parameter, with clause variations as typed conditions and group differences as lenses.
- **Reason for coarse.** Your 2026-11-12 statement: too fine a grain loses the commonality needed to unify, then specify.
- **Signs of too encompassing.** The cell's figures split systematically by setting, or a group's difference is lost. That is the reversal condition, and it shows as branches, divergence rows and contested spreads.
- **Signs of too granular.** Near-duplicate parameters sharing a kind and direction, or a parameter no two instruments can both fill.
- **Elements.** An element never earns a parameter, which is why `ramp` was declined. The promotions I made of TERM-092 and TERM-022 broke this and need undoing; the critic found the same.
- **Medical vocabulary.** Your 2026-09-11 doubt that it was "too granular to be usable" turned that lens into a demand-populated resolver, not a mirror taxonomy.

Still open: how the grain is represented (families, equivalence groups), who judges a grouping, and whether a granularity policy is doctrine or convention. The audit marks that last one as needing an owner decision.

The critic's repairs to the Edmonton digest are in progress. The scratch database refuses to amend a figure while it sits in a live determination, so I retire the ten engine cells, amend, and re-run the engine. I'll report what changed.

Different parameters that belong together are combined by an element-level determination assembled from their own determinations. The plan has the task for it, T-060, but it is not built.

**What the pieces are**
- **Parameters stay separate.** Stair width, handrail height and handrail diameter each remain a parameter with their own determination, because the split test keeps different quantities apart.
- **Element-level determination.** You answered OR-14b: the specifications pass writes an element-level determination from the related parameters' determinations. It is a new stage output, a table and a rule version, built in a tooling pull request. The element is a view over them and is never a container that figures are filed into.
- **How a parameter reaches an element.** Through typed term pointers, many to many (OD-24). A parameter needs no element.
- **Typed edges between figures.** `condition_on` and `derived_from` carry a dependency between figures, even across parameters (item 4.7 below).
- **Narrative links.** `connections` rows, of the cross-parameter or compound-interaction types, record the narrative of why parameters belong together.
- **What T-060 does with them.** The element page reads the typed edges and the connections to show how the parameters relate.

**An example from the Edmonton PDF**
- Item 4.7 says a stair needs a handrail on one side, but handrails on both sides if the stair is 1100 mm or wider. The 1100 mm is a condition on the handrail requirement, not a standalone stair-width parameter. The writer would file it as a `condition_on` edge between figures.
- Items 7.1 and 7.3 give handrail diameter (30 to 43 mm) and height (865 to 965 mm). Each is a separate quantity and so a separate parameter, and both sit under the element "handrail".
- The element-level determination for "stair" would list stair width, rise and run and the handrail parameters together, with the width-to-handrail condition shown, and would assign no value of its own.

**Where it stands today**
- **Nothing reads the links.** The skill says no code reads `connections` or `conflicts`, and the only reader is the operator at the adversarial pass. Whether the engine should consume them is an open owner question (OQ 12 of the 2026-11-06 round-3 adjudication).
- **T-060 is blocked.** Its design file isn't written and it waits on T-019 and T-029. T-037, the render, waits on it.
- **The parameters aren't in the catalogue yet.** Stair width, handrail height and diameter are among the 57 deferred phrases, so this example can't run until they are minted.

I'm continuing the critic's repairs to the Edmonton digest, with the ten engine cells retired first.

# Hand-off for adjudication and reconciliation: the Edmonton checklist digest and the owner's questions about it

Written 2026-11-13 by the coordinating session (Sonnet-class). The owner's instruction, verbatim: *"pass off all of my questions and your answers about Edmonton PDT to Fable for adjudication and reconciliation with aim to incorporate into pipeline with view of ensuring best long-term integrity of project, legibility and logical coherence, and disability coverage."* (PDT is read as PDF.)

You are the adjudicator. The coordinator's answers below are **claims to test against the repository, not findings**: several were written from a partial read and at least two contain errors the coordinator already knows of (marked). You read, verify and rule on what is the coordinator's to rule on; what is the owner's (doctrine: a tier, a vocabulary, a population term, what counts as best practice, jurisdiction, licensing) you mark **WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER** with the exact question and the ledger lines it rests on. `CLAUDE.md` governs; read it first (rule 0: a live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches; rule 5: one home per fact; rule 7a: no hand-typed counts, write the command; rule 8: derive, do not curate; rule 10: research and tooling ship apart; section 8: nothing is added without naming what reads it and what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it).

## 0. What exists to read
- The digest and its report: `scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/DIGEST-REPORT.md` (the document the owner asked for; written before the critic returned). Its drivers and logs are in the same folder (`helpers/`, `digest-log.jsonl`, `items.json`, `batch.sql`, `checks-after-*.txt`, `cell-*.json`). The payload and renders: `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/` (PDF 1a117aff4c5947a8.pdf; renders p0000 to p0008 are ZERO-BASED, PDF page N is p000(N-1); derived text with page markers).
- The scratch database the digest wrote (open read-only, never write it): `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/5dbc61f3-e21d-5874-a6a8-3a991f0f402c/scratchpad/edm/guidebook.db`. The canonical `data/guidebook.db` was never touched.
- The independent critic's report on the digest is saved in section 4 below.
- The plan: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`, `OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md`, the task files in `tasks/` (including the 20 authored this session: T-061 to T-063, T-067 to T-072, T-075 to T-085, and T-057, T-059, T-060). **An integrator agent is editing the plan index and the open-items plan right now: do not edit any of those files; you may read them, and what you read may change under you.**
- The ledger `references/project-standards.md`: use `git grep` (the Grep tool does not see parts of the repository). Anchors the coordinator found: base building three levels (line near 2053, "base_building is THREE levels"); OT-1/OT-2 on "barrier-free path of travel" (lines near 4786 and 6195); OD-24 "flat and coarse" and the split test (line near 5643); the 2026-11-12 grain statement (near 5249); the medical lens demand-populated (near 2954); OR-14b (near 6189); OR-13, OR-17; the floor-marker rulings (search `OR-7`, `code_floor_only`, "Owner rulings 2026-10-30").
- Doctrine files: `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md`, `governance/tier-system.md`, `governance/conceptual-model.md` (ENT-16 Building Type, deferred), `governance/adversarial-use-framework.md` (the three-tier design hierarchy: Universal Mode, population, person), `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`.

## 1. What the digest was (one paragraph)
The owner supplied a 9-page City of Edmonton Accessibility Advisory Committee checklist PDF and asked for a research pass, then for it to be digested "following the pipeline rules" (variant `from-evidence`). The coordinator admitted it as REF-01037 (tier 3, grey), observed and adjudicated 86 concept phrases (none minted), declined 14 and promoted 2 existing terms to parameters, wrote 16 extractions against 10 parameters with lens links, ran the engine for 10 cells (all pending), and filed gaps; a critic then attacked it (section 4). The critic's repairs are NOT yet applied on the scratch database (the writer refuses to amend a figure that sits in a live determination, so the ten engine cells must be retired, the figures amended, and the engine re-run; this was in progress). Nothing is committed, nothing is in the canonical database.

## 2. The owner's questions, in order, verbatim
Framing messages first:
- "perform a research pass on this PDF. what do you extract? give me a document with everything you did"
- "use the research approach from pipeline."
- "ie how would you digest this PDF in pipeline"
- "again, you are treating this PDF as if it came up in a research sweep"
- "you must digest it following the pipeline rules"
- "show me a report of what you did for the digest including results"

Then the questions:
- **Q1.** "best practice is the best/most forgiving/etc of all values/approaches for a given term. isn't it presumptuous to have a best practice column at this stage? differentiate as code floor vs above code floor"
- **Q2.** "what does the workplan plan to do to address all the parameters/subjects within this PDF that are not currently defined as a term in base?"
- **Q3.** "how do we dynamically improve our base for terminology/parameters/concepts?"
- **Q4.** "how do we ensure that we aren't duplicating if we add dynamically, ie find equivalencies and synonyms?"
- **Q5.** "how do we differentiate between something as a clause/branch/subitem for a term/parameter versus its own?"
- **Q6.** "how do you handle different values for a parameter based upon different access needs/ICF codes/identities? or different design modes of universal vs population vs person specific?"
- **Q7.** "how do you handle a commercial versus residential versus public?"
- **Q8.** "and how do you handle whether something is too granular to be valuable versus too encompassing to be useful?"
- **Q9.** "how do you combine things like stair widths and handrails? different parameters, but belonging together in specification?"

## 3. The coordinator's answers, as given (to be tested)

### A1 (to Q1): agreed and corrected
The coordinator had filed GAP-103 proposing a typed "Code vs Best Practice" column. On the owner's point it conceded: best practice is the guidebook's determination (the most accommodating value or approach across all values for a term), not a label on an input, so a column by that name presumes the result. It appended a correction to GAP-103 and rewrote the report's open question as: code floor versus above code floor (the document's blue "Code (required)" statements restate what it attributes to the Alberta building code; its magenta "Best Practice" statements are the committee's own recommendations beyond it), with the open question whether that is a typed property of a figure at all or is derived against the code stratum (rule 8), and what to call a figure from a non-regulatory source that restates the floor.

### A2 (to Q2): the workplan leaves most of them unaddressed
T-072 (D-8, OR-13 "from the codes held") seeds new quantities, but only from the in-scope held regulatory codes read in full with an open pass (T-105); T-020, T-028 and T-109 supply the machinery for a new parameter (quantity kind with an observation as warrant; term named by the observed phrase; kinds for live parameters); T-105 and T-031 supply the full reading and open pass; T-069 promotes adjudicated non-English observations to aliases. REF-01037 is a grey tier-3 document outside T-072's subject. Nothing in T-105, T-020, T-028 or T-072 revisits observations adjudicated DEFERRED (T-072 handles unadjudicated ones and leftover NAMES-NEW terms), so the 57 phrases deferred from this PDF have no route to becoming parameters except the standing rule that minting happens in the data pull request the owner reads (OR-17). Proposal: widen T-072's subject, or add a sibling task, to cover every DEFERRED or unadjudicated observation from any source: mint a term and parameter, adjudicate as alias or element, or decline; run after T-072; new quantity kinds put to the owner as T-072 does.

### A3 (to Q3): how the base grows dynamically
Today's mechanism: (1) harvest every concept phrase at every reading (`observe-term`, verbatim, sentence, locator; R11); (2) adjudicate each (names existing, not ours, deferred; a term is minted only from an observation, in the source's own words, never a phrase the model generates: OR-17, E1); (3) promote or decline (`add-parameter`, `decline-parameter`, `rename-term`, `merge-parameter`); (4) re-read debt is automatic (a new parameter widens the catalogue version and `v_scan_ledger` owes a targeted re-read of every held source); (5) guards (near-duplicate refusal, flat and coarse parameters OD-24, a kind needs a warrant T-020). Where it stalls: DEFERRED has no consumer; T-072 only seeds from regulatory codes; no recurrence signal; minting waits for a hand-built review; pending cells do not feed back. Proposal in order of value: a derived candidate queue (every unminted observation grouped by phrase and concept with figures, number of independent sources, their tiers, locators; recurrence across independent sources with a stated figure ranks first), a generated review sheet for the owner's bulk reading, a standing catalogue-growth batch (T-072 widened), and a feedback hook so a cell pending for a missing parameter writes a candidate back. Decisions put to the owner: is recurrence enough to propose minting (owner still approves); should an element-only phrase with no figure ever be mined; what cadence or threshold triggers a batch. Coordinator's leaning: recurrence as a ranking signal only, element-only phrases not mined, a growth batch whenever the queue holds a stated figure no parameter takes.

### A4 (to Q4): not duplicating
What exists: `add-term` compares the new name against every term and every attested English alias (`_near_terms` in `scripts/db.py`; token-set subset or superset, a one-token term inside a compound does not count) and refuses unless each match is named `--distinct-from` with a rationale; an exact name hit goes to the existing term; aliases are typed (SYNONYM, BROADER, NARROWER, TRANSLATION, DOMAIN, DEPRECATED) with an attestation (instrument, model_seed, other_source, owner_supplied, unrecorded), a model_seed alias blocks nothing; `merge-parameter` and `rename-term` undo a duplicate afterwards. What it misses: it compares words only (a synonym with no shared token is not caught), names only (not definitions, quantity kinds or units), no cross-language synonyms (E1: an instrument's own phrase counts as the name). Equivalence is a recorded judgment with a rationale; in the digest, adjudicating "doorway clearance" as existing term TERM-021 (door width) was one such judgment and is contestable. Proposed: a derived candidate list beside each proposed term, ranked by overlap of name, definition, quantity kind, unit dimension and direction (depends on T-020, T-028). The coordinator did not check whether `rename-term`, `merge-parameter` or the alias types behave exactly as stated beyond reading the help and `_near_terms`.

### A5 (to Q5): branch of a parameter versus its own
Coordinator's table: same quantity (same kind and unit dimension, same better-direction), different circumstance: same parameter, circumstance goes in `--setting`, lens, device class, or an element pointer (T-060); applies only under a condition: a branch of the determination via a `condition_on` edge (T-017 keeps it out of the headline); different quantity (width vs height vs length vs time vs count vs force): its own parameter even on the same element; a thing, not a measure: declined as an element (`decline-parameter`, the TERM-089 `ramp` precedent); a threshold that triggers a rule: a condition on that rule's figure, not a value of anything; a passage in the source: neither, clauses are what is read (clause inventory behind T-031, OD-23). Examples from the PDF: path width 1500 (item 1.2) and corridor 1100 (item 2.10) one quantity two settings (parameter 4); elevator door 910 to 915 is parameter 9 in an elevator setting; the 9 m landing interval is parameter 12; "handrails on both sides if the stair is 1100 mm or wider" is a condition on a handrail rule, not a stair-width parameter; the access aisle's 1500 and 6000 are two quantities, width and length. **Known error in the digest, admitted in this answer:** the coordinator promoted TERM-092 `intermediate landing` and TERM-022 `level threshold` to parameters (13 and 14); both names are elements, not quantities, contradicting the TERM-089 decline reasoning; the critic found the same.

### A6 (to Q6): values per group and design modes

content.text:
The layer framing fits, with one adjustment: I'd place the three parts of the mechanism at different layers.

- **Layer 2, the stage-pair protocol.** Each hand-off between stages (evidence to judgment, judgment to synthesis and so on) either acknowledges a write or refuses it. A refusal parks the content with its stage-specific class and triage steps. For example, the evidence stage has a retrieval block (Wayback) and the judgment stage has a lens warrant refusal. The repository already has the hand-off contracts that this extends: `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`, `judgment_handoff_shape.py` and `derivation_handshake_integrity`.
- **Layer 1, shared plumbing.** There is one capture point, the `dbcore.Refusal` exception, and one register entry shape, so every stage logs refusals the same way. This part belongs to orchestration.
- **Layer 0, the check.** A definition-of-done rule requires every refusal in a session to be disposed of as retried, corrected, parked with a gap, or waived with a reason. That is what lets work continue without anyone being held up.

I checked the current gap. The command log keeps each command and a hash of its output, but not the output itself. The Edmonton session's log of 295 commands holds no `REFUSING` line, so refusals leave nothing recorded today.

The mechanism stays inside rules 3 and 10 if "by hand" means an agent with context writes the intended row, the refusal, its class and a proposed amendment into the register. The content then waits for replay through the sanctioned writers once the tooling fix merges. If you meant an agent writing canonical rows by hand, that overrides rules 3 and 10 and would need your explicit ruling. I'd advise against it.

I've sent both remarks to Fable as Q10 of its adjudication, asking it to rule on the reading and on the layer split. I'll fold its answer into the plan with the rest.

156	## 2. Reconciliation: one account
157	
158	**Floor and above the floor.** A figure is recorded as its source states it, with its root. A regulatory source's figure is a floor in its jurisdiction by derivation from the source's `(evidence_type, scope)`. A grey source that repeats or attributes a code value is an echo (OR-19): its tier is unchanged and it supplies no independent root. A source's own pairing of a higher value with a floor is a relation edge. Best practice is selected by the determination as the most accommodating value in the parameter's direction; a determination resting on the regulatory stratum alone is named at ○ with the code-derived flag (OR-7; 2026-10-30). No stored property says "best practice" on an input.
159	
160	**Growth of the vocabulary.** Every reading harvests phrases; each is adjudicated; a new concept is minted as a term in the source's own words in a data pull request the owner reads (OR-17); a term becomes a parameter only when it is a quantity with a kind (T-020, T-072); an element or a method is declined and kept. A new parameter makes every held source owe a reading (`v_scan_ledger`). Parameters are seeded from the held codes (OR-13); whether another source may promote one is AQ-4.
161	
162	**Equivalence.** A phrase for a held concept is an alias with its type and attestation. Two terms for one concept are merged. Related-but-distinct concepts are term pointers (T-029). Provisions that say the same thing are synthesis relations judged at the Opus floor (T-032), proposed read-only by T-033. The writer's token guard catches shared words only; everything else is a recorded judgment.
163	
164	**Parameter, branch, or own parameter.** One measured quantity is one parameter (OD-24). A measured condition is a `condition` row on its own parameter joined by `condition_on`, and T-017 shows the conditioned claim as a branch. A thing is a term, declined. An unmeasured circumstance has no typed carrier today (AQ-3).
165	
166	**Lens and design scale.** A figure carries the group its own words name, else the group its heading names, else no identity and its ICF and access-need lenses (OD-31). `ALL` is not an identity. A determination is keyed on a parameter and at least one lens. `design_scale` is where "universal" is stated once (OD-31) and is today written from the evidence's stratum (AQ-2).
167	
168	**Building type and occupancy.** Ruled as the first of three base levels (2026-08-27); absent; held in a joined free-text cell the engine does not read.
169	
170	**Grain.** Flat and coarse, with the split test (OD-24, delegated), because the owner needs to "unify then specify". Too coarse shows as figures partitioning by circumstance; too fine as parameters no two instruments can both fill.
171	
172	**Composition.** Parameters stay separate; an element is a term reached by pointers; the specifications pass writes an element determination that points and never copies (OR-14b).

# Adjudication: the Edmonton checklist digest (REF-01037) and the owner's ten questions

Written 2026-11-13 by the adjudicator (Fable 5.2), read-only. Sources read: the hand-off, `CLAUDE.md`, the ledger by `git grep`, the scratch database (read-only), `scripts/db.py`, `scripts/dbcore.py`, `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`, `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`, the task files named below, the PDF text layer and renders p0000, p0001, p0004, p0005. Line numbers are as read on that date; each is given with a grep that finds it again. Counts are given as commands (rule 7a); where a figure is printed it is dated and the command is beside it.

`S` below is the scratch database: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/5dbc61f3-e21d-5874-a6a8-3a991f0f402c/scratchpad/edm/guidebook.db`.

## 0. Verdict

1. **The digest should not be repaired in place. Replay it on a fresh scratch copy.** Nothing is committed, the drivers are on disk (`helpers/obs.py`, `obs2.py`, `ext.py`), and an in-place repair would carry into the emitted migration two retired parameters with burnt ids, retired cells, retired `ALL` links, amended comparators and an `absent` row that cannot be retired. `CLAUDE.md` rule 3's "fix forward" binds committed migrations only.
2. **Of the nine answers: A1, A3, A4 stand with corrections; A2, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 are corrected; none is withdrawn whole.** The largest errors are in the digest itself, not the answers: it wrote the identity `ALL` against OD-31, wrote no ICF or access-need link at all, pre-empted two owner rulings on "barrier-free path of travel", and promoted two elements.
3. **Most of what the owner's questions ask for is already ruled or already tasked.** The gaps are four: `DEFERRED` has no reader; `design_scale` carries two meanings; a figure's circumstance (building type, new or existing, interior or exterior) sits in a joined free-text cell the engine never reads; and a figure whose clause names no one has no lawful lens. Three of those need the owner.
4. **Coverage.** The catalogue can hold almost none of what this document says for blind, Deaf, cognitive or invisible access needs. That is derivable today by one query (section 3) and is the finding the exercise is most useful for.
5. **Q10** (added by the coordinator): the rules support the register reading. A hand-written canonical row would override rules 3 and 10 and is left as an open owner question.

Eight owner questions are raised (section 5.3), all left OPEN.

---

## 1. Adjudication of each question and answer

### Q1 / A1. Code floor versus above the floor — STANDS, with one correction and one question withdrawn from the owner

**Premise check.** No best-practice column exists in the schema (`PRAGMA table_info(source_value_extractions)`). The "column" was a column of the report's table and a proposal in GAP-103. The owner's point holds against both.

**The owner's rule, in the owner's words** (`git grep -n -F 'best practice = the best way to do something' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 4820 and the lines after it): "best practice = the best way to do something according to how it benefits the intended group"; "best practice =/= most common or agreed upon"; "the gentlest value is the gentlest value. the evidence is that it exists in practice". Best practice is therefore an output of the determination, selected in the parameter's recorded direction. A1 is right to concede.

**Correction: A1 leaves open something that is already derivable or ruled.**
- Floor or above-floor is not a property to type on a figure. It is derived: a figure is a floor when its source is in the regulatory stratum (`db._regulatory_pairs()`), or when it echoes one; "above the floor" is a comparison on the parameter's scale (`dbcore.bound_on_scale`) against the regulatory figures of the same parameter and jurisdiction. Rule 8 forbids a curated column for it.
- What the source's blue marking adds is an **attribution**: the source says the figure is the Alberta code's. That is root genealogy, and its homes exist: `root_type`, `root_ref_id`, `root_classification_basis`. The owner has ruled on the case: OR-19, "Yes, presume an echo" (`git grep -n -F 'OR-19: "Yes, presume an echo"' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 4717; reading at 4754: "presumed to echo the code, without being re-tiered, and the presumption can be rebutted").
- So **the critic's withheld question "wrapper or root" is not the owner's: it is answered.** The wrapper keeps its tier (T3 grey); the blue figures are presumed echoes and supply no independent root. Because the Alberta code is not held, they are `untraced` with the basis sentence (precedent: extractions 57 and 64) and a lead; T-071 step 3 re-roots them when the code is admitted.
- The relation of a magenta figure to the blue figure beside it (1800 against 1100; 920 against 850) is the source's own pairing and has a typed home: an `extraction_relations` edge. None was written (`select count(*) from extraction_relations r join source_value_extractions e on e.extraction_id=r.from_extraction_id where e.ref_id='REF-01037'` on `S`).
- GAP-103 should be closed as answered by derivation, not left as a schema proposal.

**A pull-apart A1 did not see.** `governance/adversarial-use-framework.md` line 31 (`grep -n 'never \*best practice\*' governance/adversarial-use-framework.md`) says Universal Mode is "never *best practice*". The 2026-10-30 rulings name the gentlest code value as best practice at ○ with the code-derived flag (ACTION 1 of that entry; ratified by "Yes, keep the ○ band and flag", line 4873). The ruling wins (rule 0). The framework sentence is a prose caller. [NOT VERIFIED: whether it carries a supersession mark.]

### Q2 / A2. Subjects in the PDF with no base term — CORRECTED

What stands: T-072's subject is the regulatory stratum only (its section 4 item 1), REF-01037 is outside it, and no code, view, check, skill line or task reads a `DEFERRED` adjudication (`git grep -n -E "'DEFERRED'|\"DEFERRED\"" -- scripts governance/check-registry.yaml governance/pipeline-contract.yaml ':!scripts/migrations'` returns only the writer's message). The skill's resume list names unadjudicated observations and NAMES-NEW terms, not deferred ones (`grep -n 'Resume from live state' -A6 skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`).

What is wrong:
1. **"OR-17 leaves minting to the data pull request" is not a reason to defer; this digest is a data batch.** OR-17 in the owner's words (line 4713): "Yes, bulk, with me reading the PR — Ensure that these phrases/names/aliases are all present in their prescribed jurisdiction/language. It is not acceptable for the model to generate its own phrases/names/aliases." It sets conditions on minting; it does not postpone it. The skill says the same (`grep -n 'A new concept arises while a source is in hand' skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`). The critic's F16 is sustained.
2. **`DEFERRED` was used for two different states.** The schema defines it as "cannot be settled on this source alone" (`term_adjudications` DDL comment). "Handrail height" is settled on this source: it names a quantity the catalogue lacks. "Colour contrast" against LRV contrast is the genuinely unsettled kind. The first kind has a home that already has a reader: mint the **term** (not the parameter) with `add-term --from-observation`; a NAMES-NEW term that is neither a parameter nor declined is on the skill's resume list and is T-072 section 4 item 6's subject.
3. **The proposal to widen T-072 to every source pulls against OR-13** ("From the codes held", line 4677; reading at 4698: "seeded by an open-pass scan of the bucket 1 and 2 codes already held, not slug by slug"). Whether a non-code source may promote a *parameter* is not ruled. It is put to the owner as AQ-4. Minting the *term* is within the standing rule.
4. The count "57" is a result. The command: `with latest as (select a.* from term_adjudications a where a.adjudication_id=(select max(adjudication_id) from term_adjudications b where b.observation_id=a.observation_id)) select coalesce(l.outcome,'UNADJUDICATED'), count(*) from observed_terms o left join latest l using(observation_id) where o.ref_id='REF-01037' group by 1`.

### Q3 / A3. Growing the base dynamically — STANDS, with the proposal reduced

The five steps of today's mechanism are verified: the four outcomes are the column's CHECK; `v_scan_ledger` owes a reading for every source against every active parameter and a catalogue reading covers a parameter only when `catalogue_version >= parameter_id` (view header), so a new parameter creates re-read debt mechanically; `_near_terms` is the duplicate guard.

Reduced, by section 8's order:
- **Candidate queue.** Do not build a table or a ranking. The unadjudicated and deferred observations are already rows; what is missing is one read. T-079 is building `v_deferred_acts` for searches, mining and readings (`grep -n 'v_deferred_acts' workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-079-deferred-acts-with-age.md`); a deferred adjudication is a fourth kind of the same thing and rests on the same owner sentence, "deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually". Extend that view. See P3.
- **Recurrence as a signal** is T-033's subject ("terms sharing a form", read-only candidates). No second mechanism.
- **Review sheet for the owner**: the data pull request is the review (OR-17). No generator.
- **Feedback hook from a pending cell**: not needed. A cell is keyed on a parameter, so a cell cannot be pending for a parameter that does not exist. Withdrawn.
- The three "decisions put to the owner" collapse into AQ-4.

### Q4 / A4. Not duplicating — STANDS, with two corrections

Verified in `scripts/db.py` (`grep -n 'def _near_terms' -A30 scripts/db.py`): token-set subset or superset against every canonical name and every English alias whose attestation is not `model_seed`; a one-token held name inside a compound is not a match. The alias types and attestation values are the CHECKs of `term_aliases`. `merge-parameter`, `rename-term` and `retire-parameter` exist as verbs.

Corrections:
1. **The proposed ranked candidate list is T-033**, which the plan already holds, with T-029 (term-to-term pointers) and T-028 (a concept that is not an English string) under it. Extend T-033's inputs to a proposed name; add nothing new.
2. **Three places will record "equivalent", and the plan does not say how they differ.** `term_aliases.alias_type` (a phrase to a term); T-029's kinds, which include `equivalent` and `broader` (term to term); T-032's relation kinds `equivalence`, `adjacency` (provision to provision, OD-25). Two terms that are equivalent are a dual home (rule 5): the act is a merge or an alias, never a standing pointer. Smallest reconciliation: a convention in T-029's design that its `equivalent` kind is either dropped or defined as "counterpart, not identical", and one sentence naming each table's subject. No owner question.

The digest's own equivalence judgments are weaker than A4 admits. The critic's F12 list is sustained, and observation 110 ("ACCESSIBLE WASHROOM STALL" to TERM-009 accessible bathroom) is a stall adjudicated to a room.

### Q5 / A5. Branch, clause or own parameter — CORRECTED in mechanism

The table's principle matches OD-24 (`git grep -n -F 'OD-24: flat and coarse' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 5643; "two cases are two parameters only when they cannot be placed on one scale or their accessibility directions differ"). OD-24 is a delegated resolution, "not the owner's words; standing until the owner reverses it"; A5 should say so.

Corrections:
1. **"A condition on a handrail rule, not a stair-width parameter" is wrong as mechanism.** A `condition_on` edge needs a row at both ends (`extraction_relations` DDL: "this figure only holds given a second figure this project also holds as a row"), and every extraction row has `parameter_id NOT NULL`. So the 1100 mm is a row of `figure_role='condition'` **on a stair-width parameter**, which never anchors. The stair-width parameter must exist for the condition to be typed.
2. **"Handrails on one side or both" is a count.** The kinds OD-24 lists are length, gradient, force, time, luminous reflectance and its contrast, colour temperature. A new kind is added by data with a warrant and, by T-072 item 5, the owner's approval. A5 lists "count" as if it were held.
3. **"A circumstance goes in `--setting`" is today's practice and is the defect, not the answer.** See Q7.
4. The element pointer is T-029's, not T-060's.
5. The admitted error (parameters 13 and 14) is confirmed and worse than stated: TERM-092 is named in E2 as one of the terms "that carry a name no source used", to be renamed in a research pull request (`git grep -n '^| E2 ' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 5050), and it is T-072 item 6's to judge. The promotion pre-empted both.

### Q6 / A6. Values per group, and design modes — CORRECTED

Verified: the determination's key and its "at least one lens" CHECK (`specifications` DDL); a figure reaches a cell only through its live lens links (`grep -n 'a figure reaches' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`); a contested direction prints the spread (`grep -n 'direction == "contested"' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`); the engine sets `design_scale` to `universal` only on a regulatory-only basis (`grep -n 'design_scale = SCALE_UNIVERSAL' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`) and never writes `person`.

Corrections:
1. **A6 omits the ruling that governs the question.** OD-31 (`git grep -n -F 'OD-31: a provision that names no one' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 6044): "a provision that names no one carries the group its heading names (under a mobility heading, the parent MOB with no child; under a general disability heading, no identity, only its ICF and access-need lenses); ALL leaves the identity lens, universal being stated once, by design_scale". ACTION: "do not use `ALL` as an identity".
2. **`design_scale` holds two meanings.** The engine's G1 writes `universal` for "rests on codes only". OD-31 makes `universal` mean "names no group". The scratch database shows the collision: a `MOB` cell reads `universal` and an `ALL` cell reads `population` (`select parameter_id, identity_code, design_scale, regulatory_stratum_only from specifications where retired_at is null` on `S`). The code-only fact already has its own column, `regulatory_stratum_only`, so `design_scale` repeats it (rule 5) and has no room for OD-31's meaning. T-056 item 3 changes how a universal determination gathers and does not touch G1. This is AQ-2.
3. **"No rule derives a universal value from the per-group cells" is correct and is not a gap.** The ledger's first design-mode rule (line 14) defines Universal Mode as "Universal Design / Code Compliance (population-agnostic, fixed values)" and Population Mode as ranges. A universal value is not an aggregate of group values under either meaning.
4. **The lens is almost never ICF or access need.** `select (icf_code is not null), (needs_code is not null), (identity_code is not null), count(*) from v_live_lens_links group by 1,2,3` on `S` (2026-11-13: one ICF link, three access-need links, the rest identity). The answer describes four lenses; the data use one. `CLAUDE.md` section 6 requires the ICF and access-need frame.

### Q7 / A7. Commercial, residential, public — CORRECTED and completed

Verified: the 2026-08-27 ruling and its three levels (`git grep -n -F 'base_building' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 2053; the owner's words at 2056); ENT-16 is "Deferred" (`grep -n 'ENT-16' governance/conceptual-model.md`); `rooms` is the only level present.

The two items A7 could not verify:
- **`room_items` no longer exists**, and nothing references `rooms`: `select name, type from sqlite_master where sql like '%room%'` returns the `rooms` table alone. The ruling's ACTION ("`room_items` is the existing one and is re-pointed, not replaced") names an object that is gone.
- **No figure carries a typed building type.** The circumstance is in `setting`, and the project's own census flags that column as holding joined values: `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=<db> python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py | grep setting`. Door width shows it plainly: `select setting from source_value_extractions where parameter_id=9` returns values such as "new buildings; external doors to buildings used by the general public" and "existing buildings; straight-on approach": construction status, approach geometry and building use in one cell, against the 2026-11-06 schema-shape ruling (one value per cell).
- The engine does not read `setting` (`grep -n 'setting' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`: one docstring line). So A7's consequence is confirmed: a dwelling figure and a public-building figure for one parameter and lens compose into one headline.

Correction: "OD-24 says carry such variations as typed conditions; T-017 turns a conditioned claim into a branch" does not reach this case. T-017's branch is a `condition_on` edge between two rows on parameters. Building type is not a quantity, so it cannot be a condition row. **"Typed condition" has a carrier only for conditions that are themselves measured.** This is the real distance between OD-24 and the building ruling. AQ-3.

"Public" is not one of the owner's examples of a building type ("residential, commercial"); in the held sources it is a legal scope phrase that differs by instrument.

### Q8 / A8. Too granular or too encompassing — STANDS, one stale statement corrected

The split test, the reversal condition and the medical-lens history are quoted correctly (lines 5643 to 5649; 2956; 3016).

Correction: A8 lists as open "how the grain is represented, who judges a grouping, and whether a granularity policy is doctrine". Those were left open by the owner's statement (line 5247 and its "What it does not decide") and were then **resolved under delegation the same day** by OD-24: flat, families by typed term pointers, no element required (`git grep -n 'OD-24 STATUS' -- references/project-standards.md`: "RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"). Who judges a relation is OD-25 through T-032 (an Opus-class judge). What remains the owner's is the option to reverse.

Two signs A8 should add, both derivable: a parameter whose `setting` values partition its figures (too encompassing; see Q7), and a parameter with no figure from any lens but one (section 3).

### Q9 / A9. Parameters that belong together — STANDS, with corrections

OR-14b is quoted correctly (`git grep -n -F 'OR-14b — who writes an element page' -- references/project-standards.md`, line 6189), including "The element is still never a container that figures are filed into". T-060 stops on its design file. The skill line on `connections` and `conflicts` having no reader is verified (`grep -n 'No code reads' skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`).

Corrections:
1. `connections` is to be reshaped by T-032 into one relation home with kinds `equivalence`, `commonality`, `similarity`, `adjacency` (OD-25); A9 describes the table as it is, not as tasked. The element-to-parameter pointer is T-029's `element has parameter`.
2. **Two homes for "element" are in play.** The 2026-08-27 ruling orders a `base_elements` table. OR-14 (2026-10-29, line 4699) derives an element page "from a typed term pointer", OD-24 says "elements reach parameters by term pointers", and the catalogue already holds elements as terms declined as parameters (TERM-089 `ramp`). AQ-3 part (b).
3. **What an element determination may hold** follows from OR-14b and rule 5, and Edmonton supplies the test: items 4.7 and 7.1 state a rule that belongs to no single parameter (handrails on both sides when the stair is 1100 mm or wider). The element row may hold pointers to its parameters' determinations and pointers to the relation and condition rows that cross them, and nothing else. A value column on it would be a copy. This is a constraint for `T-060-design.md`, not an owner question.

### Q10. A register for what the pipeline cannot execute — the register reading is the one the rules support

The owner's words, as relayed by the coordinator (not yet in the ledger): "it may be worthwhile to have a mechanism whereby when our scripting/pipeline cannot execute something, we explicitly flag it as a gap/issue for future resolution in a register alongside having an agent fix it by hand with correct context so we aren't losing content alongside filling in its resolution and proposed amendments for that gap/issue in register"; "that way we aren't held up"; "it could be like a layer 2 protocol or something".

**Ruling on the two readings.**
- Rule 3: "Never write `data/guidebook.db` directly. Migrations only". Section 4: "Do not hand-write SQL against a table the CLI can reach. If you find one it cannot, that is a coverage bug to fix, not a licence to bypass." Rule 10: a writer gap "is filed as a GAP and either left unwritten or written through verbs the CLI already has; it is never patched with hand SQL disguised inside the batch's data migration", with batch 20 as its proof.
- These leave exactly two lawful acts when a writer refuses: write through an existing verb, or park. **The coordinator's reading (an agent with context writes the intended row, the refusal, its class and a proposed amendment into a register, and the content is replayed through the sanctioned writer after the tooling merges) is inside the rules.** It is also what "so we aren't losing content" and "that way we aren't held up" ask for.
- The other reading (an agent writes the canonical row by hand) contradicts rules 3 and 10. A live owner statement would supersede them on contact (rule 0), but the words do not say "into the database", and a rule is not read as overturned by an ambiguous phrase. It is AQ-8, OPEN.

**Facts checked.**
- The command log keeps the command and hashes, not output: keys of a line are `bytes, command, cwd, exit, interrupted, is_error, response_keys, session_id, stderr_bytes, stderr_sha256, stdout_sha256, tool, ts` (`python3 -c "import json;print(sorted(json.loads(open('scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/commands.jsonl').readline())))"`). A refusal's sentence is therefore lost. `exit` is not reliable (the hook's own comment, `grep -n 'MEASURED CORRECTION' .claude/hooks/record-command.py`), so refusals cannot be recovered from exit codes either.
- **"`dbcore.Refusal` is the single exception class" is not quite right**: `grep -n '^class Refusal' scripts/dbcore.py scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` finds two. `db.py` catches at one point (`grep -n 'except Refusal as exc' scripts/db.py`).
- `gaps` has no payload column (DDL); categories are the CHECK's.

**What the digest shows.** Two different losses, and only one of them is a refusal:
- (i) *A writer refused.* The command and the sentence are the content at risk.
- (ii) *No verb could hold it.* Nothing was attempted, so nothing is captured at a refusal point. For this kind the homes mostly exist and were not used: a figure for no parameter is already held verbatim with its locator and quote as an **observation**; a harm statement tied to no parameter has the R7 route (search flag plus GAP); the per-statement marking is root genealogy and relation edges (Q1). What is missing for (ii) is a reader for parked observations (P3), not a new store.

**Smallest mechanism, by section 8's order.**
1. *Do nothing*: fails for (i); the sentence is gone and the retry history with it.
2. *Convention*: a rule in `/batch-done` that every refusal met in the batch is listed with one disposition: **retried** (the writer was right and the corrected call succeeded), **parked** (a gap id), or **waived** (with a reason). This is the definition-of-done part and needs no code.
3. *Reuse*: the register is the `gaps` table (`add-gap`, category by the CHECK; T-013 is already typing gaps). The payload's home is the captured line itself, since the refused argv **is** the replay command. No payload column and no new table until a reader needs to query payloads across sessions; today the reader is the tooling task that closes the gap and the research batch that replays.
4. *Smallest code*: at `db.py`'s one catch point (and the engine's), append one JSON line to `scratchpad/<CURRENT>/refusals.jsonl`: time, verb, argv, the refusal sentence. It rides rule 6's commit of the scratchpad. A handful of lines; it replaces nothing and makes nothing deletable, so it must be justified by its reader: `/batch-done`'s disposition list and the replay.

## 2. Reconciliation: one account

**Floor and above the floor.** A figure is recorded as its source states it, with its root. A regulatory source's figure is a floor in its jurisdiction by derivation from the source's `(evidence_type, scope)`. A grey source that repeats or attributes a code value is an echo (OR-19): its tier is unchanged and it supplies no independent root. A source's own pairing of a higher value with a floor is a relation edge. Best practice is selected by the determination as the most accommodating value in the parameter's direction; a determination resting on the regulatory stratum alone is named at ○ with the code-derived flag (OR-7; 2026-10-30). No stored property says "best practice" on an input.

**Growth of the vocabulary.** Every reading harvests phrases; each is adjudicated; a new concept is minted as a term in the source's own words in a data pull request the owner reads (OR-17); a term becomes a parameter only when it is a quantity with a kind (T-020, T-072); an element or a method is declined and kept. A new parameter makes every held source owe a reading (`v_scan_ledger`). Parameters are seeded from the held codes (OR-13); whether another source may promote one is AQ-4.

**Equivalence.** A phrase for a held concept is an alias with its type and attestation. Two terms for one concept are merged. Related-but-distinct concepts are term pointers (T-029). Provisions that say the same thing are synthesis relations judged at the Opus floor (T-032), proposed read-only by T-033. The writer's token guard catches shared words only; everything else is a recorded judgment.

**Parameter, branch, or own parameter.** One measured quantity is one parameter (OD-24). A measured condition is a `condition` row on its own parameter joined by `condition_on`, and T-017 shows the conditioned claim as a branch. A thing is a term, declined. An unmeasured circumstance has no typed carrier today (AQ-3).

**Lens and design scale.** A figure carries the group its own words name, else the group its heading names, else no identity and its ICF and access-need lenses (OD-31). `ALL` is not an identity. A determination is keyed on a parameter and at least one lens. `design_scale` is where "universal" is stated once (OD-31) and is today written from the evidence's stratum (AQ-2).

**Building type and occupancy.** Ruled as the first of three base levels (2026-08-27); absent; held in a joined free-text cell the engine does not read.

**Grain.** Flat and coarse, with the split test (OD-24, delegated), because the owner needs to "unify then specify". Too coarse shows as figures partitioning by circumstance; too fine as parameters no two instruments can both fill.

**Composition.** Parameters stay separate; an element is a term reached by pointers; the specifications pass writes an element determination that points and never copies (OR-14b).
